```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(CloneCensorWeight)
```

Running multiple analysis specifications over the same data is a core
workflow for sensitivity analyses — comparing different grace periods,
interval lengths, variance estimators, or outcome definitions without
re-extracting data from the CDM.

## Data

We use the built-in sample data for illustration.  In a real study
`createSampleCloneCensorWeightData()` is replaced by
`getDbCloneCensorWeightData()`.

```{r data}
ccwData <- createSampleCloneCensorWeightData(n = 300, seed = 42)
```

## Defining multiple analysis specifications

Each `CcwAnalysis` object captures every analytical choice: arm strategy,
interval length, IPCW settings, and outcome model.  Here we define three
analyses varying the grace period.

```{r specs}
makeAnalysis <- function(id, gracePeriod) {
  createCcwAnalysis(
    analysisId = id,
    description = paste("Grace period:", gracePeriod, "days"),
    createStudyPopulationArgs = createCreateStudyPopulationArgs(
      riskWindowEnd  = 365,
      endAnchor      = "cohort start",
      removeSubjectsWithPriorOutcome = FALSE
    ),
    createClonesAndCensorArgs = createCreateClonesAndCensorArgs(
      arms = list(
        createArmDefinition("initiate", "initiateWithin", gracePeriod = gracePeriod),
        createArmDefinition("never",    "deferBeyond",    gracePeriod = gracePeriod)
      ),
      intervalLength = 30
    ),
    createCensoringWeightsArgs = createCreateCensoringWeightsArgs(),
    fitOutcomeModelArgs        = createFitOutcomeModelArgs("cox", "robust")
  )
}

analysisList <- list(
  makeAnalysis("gp30",  gracePeriod = 30),
  makeAnalysis("gp60",  gracePeriod = 60),
  makeAnalysis("gp90",  gracePeriod = 90)
)
```

The `TargetComparatorOutcome` object links the analysis to cohort IDs.
For the sample data all subjects share `indexCohortId = 1`.

```{r tao}
tao <- createTargetComparatorOutcome(
  indexCohortId      = 1L,
  targetCohortId     = 1L,
  comparatorCohortId = 1L,
  outcomeIds         = c(1L)
)

specs <- createCcwAnalysesSpecifications(
  ccwAnalysisList      = analysisList,
  targetArmOutcomeList = list(tao)
)
```

## Running all analyses

`runCcwAnalysesOnData()` iterates over every combination of
`TargetComparatorOutcome` × `CcwAnalysis` × outcome and appends results to CSV
files in `outputFolder`.  Resume logic means a partially-completed run can
be restarted without re-doing finished analyses.

```{r run, warning=FALSE}
outputFolder <- tempfile("ccw_multi_")
suppressWarnings(
  runCcwAnalysesOnData(
    data                      = ccwData,
    ccwAnalysesSpecifications = specs,
    outputFolder              = outputFolder,
    databaseId                = "sample"
  )
)
list.files(outputFolder)
```

## Reading back results

```{r read}
results <- importFromCsv(outputFolder)
names(results)
```

The outcome model table has one row per analysis × outcome combination.

```{r om-table}
om <- results$ccw_outcome_model
om[, c("analysis_id", "model_type", "estimate", "lower_95", "upper_95", "p_value")]
```

## Comparing estimates across grace periods

```{r compare}
om$gracePeriod <- sub("gp", "", sub("_.*", "", om$analysis_id))
om$gracePeriod <- factor(om$gracePeriod, levels = c("30", "60", "90"))
om[order(om$gracePeriod), c("gracePeriod", "estimate", "lower_95", "upper_95")]
```

## Serialising the specification

The full specification can be written to JSON for sharing or version control.

```{r save-load}
analysisFile <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
saveCcwAnalysisList(analysisList, analysisFile)

reloaded <- loadCcwAnalysisList(analysisFile)
vapply(reloaded, function(a) a$analysisId, character(1))
```

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(outputFolder, recursive = TRUE)
unlink(analysisFile)
```
